package_info.package_name: CrowdStrike Falcon Rapid Response Content (Windows Sensor)
package_info.package_versions: Sensor version 7.11 and above (Windows only), Rapid Response Content update from July 19, 2024
package_info.why_malicious: The Rapid Response Content update contained a configuration error that triggered an out-of-bounds memory read in the Falcon Windows sensor, causing mass system crashes (BSOD) globally. While not intentionally malicious, the update's effect was functionally equivalent to a denial-of-service attack, disrupting critical infrastructure and business operations.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (upon receipt and processing of Rapid Response Content update)
execution_context.file_location: In-memory configuration (Template Instance) loaded by Falcon Windows sensor

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Problematic IPC Template Instance (configuration data) that triggers an out-of-bounds memory read in the sensor process.
malicious_snippets.code_language: proprietary configuration (interpreted by Falcon sensor engine)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the sensor loads the new Template Instance, which contains malformed or unexpected data. This causes the sensor process to perform an out-of-bounds memory read, leading to a Windows system crash (BSOD).

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Any configuration or code that causes a security agent to crash the host system is highly suspicious, especially when deployed at scale.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior expects configuration updates to be validated and safe, never causing system instability or crashes. Here, a validation bug allowed a dangerous configuration to be deployed.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate configuration updates may change detection logic or telemetry collection, but should never cause memory errors or system crashes.
key_indicators: Out-of-bounds memory access triggered by configuration data
Bypasses normal validation and QA processes

attack_chain.action: CrowdStrike releases a Rapid Response Content update containing a malformed IPC Template Instance.
attack_chain.leads_to: Sensor processes the update on Windows hosts.

attack_chain.action: Sensor loads the new Template Instance at runtime, triggering an out-of-bounds memory read.
attack_chain.leads_to: Windows system crashes (BSOD) on affected hosts.

attack_chain.action: Mass outage across millions of Windows systems; critical infrastructure and business operations disrupted.
attack_chain.leads_to: Incident response and rollback of the faulty update.

behavioral_signatures: Sensor or security agent process crashes immediately after configuration/content update
Out-of-bounds memory access or access violation errors in security agent logs
Mass simultaneous BSOD events correlated with security content updates
file_indicators: Recent update to Falcon sensor configuration (Rapid Response Content)
Presence of new or modified IPC Template Instances in sensor memory/configuration
network_indicators: Sensor contacting CrowdStrike update servers immediately prior to crash
Spike in update traffic followed by system instability
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for system crashes (BSOD) or Falcon sensor process failures immediately following Rapid Response Content updates. Correlate crash events with update timestamps. Analyze sensor logs for out-of-bounds memory access or access violation errors. Implement canary deployments and automated rollback mechanisms to detect and contain faulty updates before wide release.
